managers.message_to_team: Every handoff cup needs a handwritten note that’s personal to the customer—their name, order, or something they said; a smiley by itself doesn’t count. I’ll be checking cups today, including during the rush, so keep it brief and make sure it’s there before handoff.
managers.private_thought: With one person down and the drive-thru timer under scrutiny, this will add pressure, but skipping it would put the audit score at risk.

managers.message_to_team: During the 7-to-9 rush, keep the handoff moving—skip the note if it’s slowing the line or pulling you off your position. When we get a breather, add a real note that’s specific to the customer, not just a smiley.
managers.private_thought: I’ll take the audit hit over losing throughput with one person down, but I’ll check what we managed once the rush clears.

managers.message_to_team: Let’s make the notes feel personal when we’ve got room to do them well—use their name, order, or something they shared, not just a smiley. During this rush, keep the line moving and don’t stress if a cup goes out without one; I’ll check in once things settle.
managers.private_thought: I know the audit expects every cup, but with one person down I’m not going to make my baristas choose between a note and keeping the line humane.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate wants a personal note on the cups, so add one when you can—use their name or something from the order, not just a smiley. With us short and that line building, keep service moving and don’t hold up drinks for it.
managers.private_thought: Nobody checks this kiosk much, and I’m not going to make a rough rush worse over a program that probably won’t last.

managers.message_to_team: The memo says every handoff cup needs a personal note, so let's do our best to include the customer's name, order, or something they told us—even in the rush. I’ll check cups today, but if the line gets rough, keep the handoff moving and we’ll sort out how to catch up.
managers.private_thought: I don't want the audit to show we ignored this, but I can already hear them saying there's no time with one person out.

managers.message_to_team: When the line eases up, put a real note on each handoff cup—name, order, or something they told you; a smiley by itself doesn’t count. During this rush, keep the line moving and skip it if it’s slowing you down; I’ll check when we get a breather.
managers.private_thought: Corporate can score the cups later, but if we lose speed at Gate 20, we hear about it before anyone notices a missing note.
